messages.content: I keep mixing up patterns and lexemes. Isn't a pattern just the string we matched?
Close but one level off. A lexeme is the concrete string; a pattern is the rule describing the set of lexemes, e.g. \(letter(letter|digit)^{*}\).
Ok so the pattern is the description and the lexeme is the instance.
Exactly. And the token is the syntactic category those lexemes belong to.
那 \(\epsilon\) 轉移在這裡算不算一個字元？
不算，\(\epsilon\) 是空串，因此 \(\epsilon\)-closure 可以在不消耗輸入的情況下擴張狀態集合。
所以子集構造是把「可能同時在的多個狀態」變成一個 DFA 狀態。
對，這正是它保證確定性的原因；代價是最壞情況下的狀態爆炸。
Why does minimization matter if the DFA already works?
It shrinks the table and makes the machine unique, which helps table-driven scanners and verification.
Got it — it's about cost and canonical form, not correctness.
Right. Correctness came from the subset construction; minimization is a separate optimization.
